A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIA attack and TDRT defense research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are available and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack and defense experiments on Meta-World, MuJoCo, and MiniGrid, plus sensitivity analyses and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds defense comparisons, attack success rates, and attacker computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: BIA, TDRT, their objectives and pseudocode, and the GAIfO/AILBoost extensions remain unchanged. Expanded motivation and standardization of TDRT's name do not introduce a different algorithm, architecture, or training procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds reward-minimization target scenarios on the retained MuJoCo and coordinate-state MiniGrid tasks, alongside the earlier high-reward-target scenarios. The environments, Meta-World task pairs, MiniGrid sizes, and existing coordinate/RGB coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: New v3 Tables 5 and 8 evaluate SA-PPO alongside PPO and TDRT-PPO in MuJoCo and MiniGrid; v2's Appendix F compared only PPO and TDRT-PPO. The original comparisons and their comparator sets remain intact. Newly discussed diffusion and backdoor methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds defense evaluations using sufficiently trained victims and target policies trained on negated task rewards, distinct from the retained deliberately constrained-victim experiments. Appendix G.4 introduces Meta-World task-success ASR over 50 episodes at epsilon 0.3, and G.5 separately measures attack training and test costs. These substantially extend evaluation protocols without establishing changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 extends the time-discounting versus uniform-smoothing comparison to the additional MuJoCo/MiniGrid defense settings and adds attacker computational-cost analysis in G.5. Existing demonstration-count, demonstration-quality, attack-budget, regularization-strength, and defense-training-time analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing practice of reporting means and standard deviations over 50 evaluation episodes, with half-standard-deviation bands in relevant plots, is unchanged. No new training-seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: All ten v2 tables retain their numerical results, and all five figures retain their plotted evidence. New v3 Tables 5, 8, 10, and 11 add substantial defense, success-rate, and timing results. For example, BIA-ILfD ASR is 1.00 on drawer-close but 0.00 on drawer-open; its reported training time is 6.2 hours, while Targeted PGD takes 37 seconds per test episode. These are additional measurements, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1, 6.1, and C.1, the supporting lemmas and proofs, and Appendix D's derivations remain mathematically unchanged. Section 6's added discussion of setting the target reward to the negative original reward explains a special case of the retained objective.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about limited-access BIA, TDRT as a dedicated behavior-targeted defense, and preservation of original-task performance. The introduction's reported 28.2% improvement over uniform smoothing is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly relates the defense objective to reward-minimization defenses. Appendix F.2 adds a performance-ceiling explanation for similar MiniGrid results, and G.5 explains BIA's discriminator-training cost and potential amortization across attacks. The limitations concerning image inputs and lack of certified guarantees remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes the code-access link from Appendix I without providing a replacement; this changes access documentation, not demonstrably repository availability. G.5 adds attacker timing information measured on one NVIDIA H100. H.2 corrects the regularization coefficient label from gamma to lambda while retaining the sweep values and results. Architecture and tuning details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds diffusion-defense positioning as complementary to TDRT, discusses CAR-DQN and additional poisoning/backdoor work including TrojDRL and BadRL, and describes Bai et al.'s approach as preference-based reinforcement learning instead of imitation learning. It also adds the DeepSeek-R1 citation and removes the Madry reference. The central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Related work receives localized rewrites and numbered attack/defense subsections; method motivation is expanded, and acknowledgements and ethics sections are added. Terminology, grammar, cross-references, author information, and citation style are edited. The main narrative and Appendix A–I organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted into the ICLR layout, changing the title/author block, running headers, heading typography, and placement of text and displays throughout. Four tables are added, and existing displays are repositioned or resized; Figures 3 and 4 now share a page, and Algorithm 3 moves later. The underlying figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new success-rate measurements, attacker cost accounting, and SA-PPO comparisons make the unchanged claims easier to assess and provide a modest net improvement in empirical transparency. Clearer positioning and the regularization-label correction also help. These gains are tempered by removal of the code-access link and inconsistent new labels: Tables 5 and 8 say lower attack rewards are better despite upward-arrow headers, and Table 10 labels PA-AD black-box despite its retained white-box description.
